name: OProfile
listed_description: Statistical profiler for Linux. Can profile any code (including the kernel!) with low overhead and without recompilation.
reason: Directional claim only on reachable pages. The manual in the source tree (doc/oprofile.xml on sourceforge.net/p/oprofile/oprofile, last commit 2024-12-10) says 'very little overhead' and 'need low overhead' with no percentages and no gprof comparison; opgprof only exports gprof-format data. A '1-8% typical overhead' figure and a gprof '30% to 260%' instrumentation figure appeared only in WebSearch snippets that cite oprofile.sourceforge.io (EGRESS_BLOCKED), en.wikipedia.org and ics.com (both blocked) and arXiv papers (blocked); even those are two separate figures, not a measured head-to-head run against gprof. GitHub mirror github.com/oprofile/oprofile returned 404.

name: ROOT
listed_description: A set of OO frameworks with all the functionality needed to handle and analyze large amounts of data in a very efficient way.
reason: ROOT's README, tree/ntuple/doc and release notes (v6.26 to v6.40 read via raw.githubusercontent.com) carry only self-comparisons (older ROOT versions, e.g. 'likelihood minimization up to 10x faster', 'rootls 3 to 4x faster') and no external baseline. The external comparison exists in the RNTuple papers (arXiv 2204.09043 'RNTuple performance: Status and Outlook', arXiv 2501.07666): RNTuple vs TTree, HDF5 and Apache Parquet on an AMD EPYC 7702P, zstd level 5 (HDF5 zlib level 3), but arXiv, indico.jlab.org, inspirehep.net and root.cern were all EGRESS_BLOCKED, so no number could be read from an opened page. Public benchmark code is at github.com/jblomer/iotools (top level compares TTree and RNTuple only; compare/ holds TTree, HDF5 and Parquet programs for CMS and LHCb data) but the repo publishes no results. Retry with arXiv access: likely tier B (peer-reviewed proceedings) with baseline HDF5 or Parquet, category filesystems-and-io.

name: stdgpu
listed_description: Efficient STL-like Data Structures on the GPU.
reason: README makes no numeric claim ('fast and reliable data management', 'orthogonal approach' to thrust). The repo's benchmarks/stdgpu/*.inc programs (Google Benchmark style; unordered_map, unordered_set, vector, deque, bitset, mutex) time stdgpu containers only, with no baseline library. The only candidate numbers are in the author's paper 'stdgpu: Efficient STL-like Data Structures on the GPU' (arXiv 1908.05936, cited in the README), but arXiv, ar5iv, alphaxiv and hgpu.org were EGRESS_BLOCKED and WebSearch snippets held no numbers. Category fit is also doubtful: GPU hash containers belong to hash-maps-sets, not thread-pools-work-stealing. Retry with arXiv access.

name: YUP!
listed_description: The modern framework optimized for realtime audio and GPU-native creative software
reason: No benchmark or timing against any baseline anywhere reachable: README (Why YUP, platforms, examples), docs/dsp, docs/multithreading, docs/graphics and the tests/ folder list (no benchmark files) were read; docs/dsp/oscillators.md states 'No timing claims are implied by the API' and ydsp-resource-plan.md only plans benchmarks against earlier revisions of its own DSP code. 'Optimized' in the title is directional. It is a JUCE7-derived framework with the Rive renderer (ISC, 181 stars, active, last commit 2026-10-06).
